analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md, adding a paragraph at head lines 1584-1592. The paragraph says LocalTokenizerLoader resolves an absent clean_up_tokenization_spaces key to false in memory, matching Python Transformers, and keeps an explicit Boolean. It also says decode spacing does not affect input IDs, sampling or cache keys. I examined both base units (lines 838-1644). The only changed content is the documentation paragraph, and it describes no new endpoint, wire field, key handling, storage, attestation path or authorization behavior. No source code is changed here. The claim that cache keys do not depend on the setting is plausible, since the setting affects detokenization output and not encode. The cache-scope and prefix-cache posture (T-041: coordinator-authored scope, HMAC tags, 30-minute TTL) is unchanged by this text. The behavioral change it documents, in LocalTokenizerLoader.swift, was not supplied. Its effect on decoded output and streaming byte-repeat behavior can only be evaluated in that source. Relevant threat surfaces are low: output text fidelity (T-007 is about a malicious provider, not this) and tokenizer config loading from model directories (T-012 weights/config tampering by the operator is pre-existing). No regression or threat-model gap is identified from the documentation alone. A later pass that sees LocalTokenizerLoader.swift should confirm that the in-memory override does not write to the model directory, which would affect the weight-hash and prompt-contract identity, and that the prompt contract hash (PromptContractIdentity) still reads the unmodified on-disk tokenizer files.
